generators.carrier: determinant of the spin-up fermion matrix as a function of the auxiliary field configuration
determinant of the spin-down fermion matrix as a function of the auxiliary field configuration
product of spin-up and spin-down determinants as the field weight

relations.statement: At half filling on a bipartite lattice, a particle-hole transformation gives det_down(s) = det_up(s) up to a positive factor, so the weight is nonnegative.
relations.hypotheses: bipartite lattice, half filling (mu = U/2), repulsive U, Hubbard-Stratonovich decoupling in the charge/spin channel as stated by the package

relations.statement: For attractive U with spin-balanced chemical potentials, det_down(s) = conj(det_up(s)), so the weight is |det_up|^2 >= 0.
relations.hypotheses: attractive U, spin-balanced filling, density-channel decoupling with real coupling

relations.statement: The Hamiltonian-to-representation equality: the partition function equals the sum over auxiliary fields of the weight, for each stated model.
relations.hypotheses: stated model, Trotter-exact or defined discretization, including boundary cases (open/periodic)

lemmas.statement: Under r_pair_half_bipartite or r_pair_attractive hypotheses, the weight is nonnegative for every auxiliary field configuration.
Outside the protected hypotheses, there exist a model and field configuration with negative weight; this witness is distinct from the protected case.

near_misses.claim: Determinant positivity holds for the repulsive Hubbard model away from half filling.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Particle-hole pairing fails when mu differs from U/2, so det_up and det_down are not related and the sign problem appears.

near_misses.claim: Half-filled repulsive positivity holds on any lattice.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The sublattice sign transformation requires bipartiteness; frustrated hoppings break the pairing.

near_misses.claim: Attractive-U positivity holds with spin-imbalanced chemical potentials.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The conjugation pairing requires equal spin chemical potentials.
